text:
Meridian Textiles Returns to Profit After Restructuring

Meridian Textiles reported a pre-tax profit of €12.4 million for the first half, [1] a loss of €8 million in the same period last year. [2] The turnaround follows the closure of two loss-making plants and a renegotiation of supply contracts, measures that chief executive Ilse Kramer described as painful but unavoidable.

Analysts caution, [3], that the improvement may prove temporary. Cotton prices have begun to rise again, and the company has yet to find a way to [4] the effect of a ten percent increase in labor costs.

questions.explanation: 'Compared with' is the fixed expression for setting one result against another; 'on', 'in' and 'at' cannot follow 'compared' in this sense.

choices: The result marks a striking decline for a company that analysts had praised barely eighteen months ago.
The result marks a striking reversal for a company that analysts had written off barely eighteen months ago.
The result falls short of expectations for a company that analysts had forecast to double sales within eighteen months.
The result was announced by a company that analysts had written off long before the closure of its two plants.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins 'The turnaround follows', so the previous one must describe a reversal from loss to profit; the others describe a decline, a disappointment, or a timeline that clashes with 'follows the closure'.
The sentence contrasts good results with a warning; 'however' marks that contrast, whereas 'therefore', 'moreover' and 'similarly' do not.
The company must 'offset' (counterbalance) the effect of rising labor costs; 'offend' means insult, 'offer' means propose, and 'offload' means unload.

text:
Subject: Interruption to your service on 3 and 4 March

Dear Ms. Ferreira,

I am writing to apologize for the interruption to your account that began on the evening of 3 March and [1] until the following afternoon. [2] That fault has since been corrected, and the update has been withdrawn pending a full review.

I understand that the outage disrupted your quarter-end reporting, [3] we have credited your account with the equivalent of two months' fees. We have also commissioned an independent review, the findings of which will be shared with you [4] they become available.

questions.explanation: An interruption 'persisted' (continued) until the afternoon; 'persevered' describes a person's determination, 'persuaded' means convinced, and 'perpetuated' means made to continue by someone.

choices: The cause has been traced to a scheduled update to our authentication system, which was installed with sufficient testing.
The cause has been traced to a faulty update to our authentication system, which was installed without sufficient testing.
The cause has been traced to a fault in your own network, which was installed without sufficient testing by our staff.
The cause has been explained to our customers, who were informed of the update in advance of the installation.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says 'That fault has since been corrected, and the update has been withdrawn', so the previous one must identify a fault in the update; only the first does. The others describe a flawless update, blame the customer's network, or mention no fault.
The credit is a consequence of the disruption, expressed by 'as a result'; the other options express contrast, which does not fit an apology.
'As soon as they become available' gives the timing of sharing the findings; 'even if', 'whereas' and 'unless' distort that meaning.

text:
To: Warehouse and Logistics Managers
From: Teodor Maric, Health and Safety Officer
Subject: Mandatory use of protective equipment

Following the incident in Bay 4 last month, the safety committee has concluded that existing rules on protective equipment were applied inconsistently. [1] With effect from Monday, all personnel entering the loading area, [2] of their role, must wear high-visibility clothing and approved footwear.

Supervisors will be held [3] for ensuring compliance within their shifts. [4] a worker is found without the required equipment, he or she will be asked to leave the area until the omission has been corrected. Repeated failures will be dealt with under the disciplinary procedure.

choices: The committee therefore considers that a single, unambiguous standard is preferable to local arrangements that vary by team.
The committee therefore considers that a single, unambiguous standard is unnecessary given local arrangements that vary by team.
The committee therefore considers that local standards are preferable to a single rule that varies by team.
The committee has therefore concluded that arrangements that vary by team will remain in force until the next incident.
questions.explanation: The next sentence imposes one rule for 'all personnel', so the previous sentence must favor a single standard. The others call it unnecessary, prefer local rules, or keep the variation.
'Irrespective of their role' is the fixed expression meaning without regard to; 'notwithstanding', 'apart' and 'aside' are not followed by 'of' in this sense.
'Held accountable for' means made responsible for; the other forms are not adjectives that follow 'held'.
'Where a worker is found without the required equipment' introduces the specific case; 'whereas' contrasts, 'wherein' means in which, and 'whereby' means by which.

text:
Dear Dr. Okonkwo,

I am pleased to offer you the position of Senior Research Fellow in the Department of Environmental Engineering, commencing on 1 September. The appointment is for a fixed term of three years, [1] to review after the second year.

[2] Your salary will be £58,400 per annum, payable monthly in arrears, and you will be entitled to thirty days' annual leave in addition to public holidays. Should you accept this offer, you will be required to [3] the enclosed contract and return it by 15 July. [4] we have not received it by that date, we reserve the right to withdraw the offer.

Yours sincerely,
Professor Anneliese Vogt
Head of Department

questions.explanation: 'Subject to review' is the fixed expression meaning dependent on review; the other forms do not fit after the comma.

choices: The terms of the appointment are set out in full in the attached contract, of which the following are the principal exceptions.
The terms of the appointment are set out in full in the attached contract, of which the following are the principal provisions.
The terms of the appointment will be agreed in full after the attached contract, of which the following are the principal provisions.
The terms of the previous appointment are set out in full in the attached contract, of which the following were the main provisions.
questions.explanation: The next sentences list salary and leave, which are principal provisions; only the first option introduces them correctly. The others speak of exceptions, postpone the agreement, or refer to a previous appointment.
A contract is 'countersigned' after it has been signed by the other party; 'countermand' means revoke, 'counteract' means neutralize, and 'counterfeit' means forge.
'In the event that we have not received it' introduces a possible situation; 'unless' would create a double negative with 'not', 'whereas' contrasts, and 'inasmuch as' means because.
